findings.title: Cross-site refusal relies on Sec-Fetch-Site, sent only over HTTPS or localhost; password mode accepts plain HTTP
findings.reason: The owner deploys the hub only over HTTPS (tailscale serve or an HTTPS reverse proxy), where browsers send Sec-Fetch-Site; the spec and D3 now say the refusal relies on HTTPS.

findings.title: Cut-text notice of a large HTML points to «Abrir aparte», which now opens the rendered page, not the source
findings.scoreReason: The claim holds: in «Ver el texto» the notice sends you to «Abrir aparte», which for HTML now opens the rendered page, so the full source of an HTML over 2 MB cannot be read in the panel; it only affects that rare case and changing the text or the raw-mode link is a small fix, so mention it rather than open an item.

findings.title: Page-route only rule and the hook's cross-site route condition live in index.ts without unit tests
findings.scoreReason: The `grant.only` check sits inline in the handler at index.ts:1208, which the server standards forbid (feature logic belongs in modules), and if it broke quietly a page could read its sibling files; but the core `fromAnotherSite` predicate already has tests in auth.test.ts and both rules were checked with curl, so mention it, no item needed.

findings.title: Duplicate of the extension helper of shared/file-types.ts
findings.scoreReason: A four-line helper whose behaviour differs on purpose (it strips the path and lowercases), so merging the two saves almost nothing and only touches style.

findings.title: HTML viewer downloads up to 2 MB of text, waits for it before the iframe, then the iframe downloads the file again
findings.scoreReason: The claim holds: FileBody checks `text === null` before `rendersPage`, so the iframe waits for up to 2 MB of text that it then downloads again, but most HTML files are small, and the text also feeds the binary check and the «Ver el texto» toggle, so reworking it carries some risk for a modest gain.

findings.title: First test mostly restates the content-type table; name it as a deliberate pin or trim it to the cases with logic
Says browsers send Sec-Fetch-Site only over HTTPS; they also send it to localhost, as D3 says
